question: According to the report published by the Commission on 15 January 2024, steady progress was made in the implementation of the European structural and investment funds over the period 2014-2020. A wide range of investments were made, covering various programmes. More specifically, the report states that health services for more than 63 million people were improved, while 64.

5 million people found employment thanks to the implementation of the funds. Nevertheless, local and regional authorities often seemed to encounter problems receiving and using these funds, which reduced the actual implementation of the EU financing. In view of the above, what steps will the Commission take to support local authorities in the implementation of such financing?
answer: The principle of partnership is a key feature in the implementation of the common provisions regulation funds, building on the multi-level governance approach and ensuring the involvement of national, regional and local authorities, and also civil society and social partners. Each Member State must set-up a comprehensive partnership to ensure the implementation of these funds (1).

In the 2021-2027 funding period, greater emphasis to the need of engagement of local authorities was introduced, requiring the participation of local actors in the development and implementation of integrated territorial strategies. Member States can use the technical assistance budget to support the development and implementation of Cohesion Policy programmes.
The Commission has also made available a series of tools (2) to support Member States in implementing these programmes.

These tools help programme authorities to develop strategies for capacity building, to identify and address competency gaps and weaknesses in programme administration, to exchange and network with peers from other EU countries, and to learn how to better deal with challenges related to integrity and transparency, prevention of fraud and corruption, public procurement, state aid, and citizen engagement.

Furthermore, the European Social Fund+ (ESF+) Committee specifically supports the implementation of ESF+ programmes. The Commission also has a comprehensive monitoring strategy to identify and support lower-performing programmes.

According to the Common Provisions Regulation https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32021R1060 and the Code of Conduct on Partnership https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R0240 https://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/policy/how/improving-investment_en
